findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice on the sharding path, which can duplicate ad-hoc filters
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target. `runShardSplitQuery` already does the same interpolation and then passes each shard sub-request, whose targets are already interpolated, to `runSplitQuery`. The same query is therefore interpolated twice, and the passed `request.filters` are applied to the expression twice. `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent. Ad-hoc filters can be injected into the expression a second time. Interpolated values that contain `$` or `[[ ]]` sequences can be re-expanded. The updated shard test asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times, which locks in the double work instead of catching it. Interpolation should happen once, either in `runSplitQuery` only, or the already-interpolated queries should be marked and skipped.

findings.title: Assertion hard-codes 5 calls, which encodes redundant double interpolation
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` replaces the previous `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` check on `interpolateVariablesInQueries`. The count of 5 is one initial interpolation plus one per sub-request. It is a brittle number that confirms queries are re-interpolated per shard request, rather than verifying that interpolation happens once at the start. The mock also mutates the query in place, so it cannot reveal non-idempotent behaviour such as duplicated filters.
